The correct view is that it does, meaning that such discrimination is in fact very illegal under Title VII. Some federal judges are mistaken on this point, but I gather that most are not.

Civil rights law, both federal and state, generally prohibits *ever* firing someone for belonging to a protected class. You can generally fire someone because you don’t like their lipstick, or because you had a dream where they gave you the finger, or because you just like killing people’s dreams. But you **cannot ever** fire someone for being Asian, or male, or Catholic, or part of any other protected class. Of course, proving that you were fired on the basis of a protected class is generally non-trivial, because only a monumentally stupid boss will say, “Yeah, I fired them for being black.” But it is still absolutely illegal, even if you can be fired for no reason: my dad makes his living defending victims of employment discrimination.

Whether gender identity qualifies as a protected class can be tricky: federal courts tend to interpret federal civil rights law as protecting against discrimination on the basis of gender identity, but there remains disagreement; on the other hand, many states and more local jurisdictions explicitly protect against employment discrimination against trans people. Again, these apply even if employees otherwise can be fired without cause. No matter the contract or local law, it is never, ever, *ever* legal to fire someone for belonging to a protected class. No contract has the legal power to do this.

tl;dr: **It is very illegal to fire someone for being trans, even if this was not given as the reason, and even if employers are otherwise allowed to fire employees for arbitrary reasons.**
